_about: Hand-kept additions to the match rules that scripts/sync.py derives from each entry's paths.
'paths' adds to the rule made from one of a page's paths, keyed by the path as the page writes it:
beside: a file that must sit next to the folder, has: a file that must be inside it (so an ordinary
build or target folder isn't taken for Flutter's or Rust's);
verdict and note: for a folder a page lists as where the item lives, not as the item itself, such as
the Homebrew Cellar on the Homebrew cache page. The note says what the page says about that folder.
'extra' adds rules an entry's page supports but its paths don't spell out.
Every addition must be backed by the page's own text.

/opt/homebrew/Cellar.note: Don’t delete folders in the Cellar by hand: Homebrew links each installed version into its `bin` and other folders. `brew cleanup` removes old versions, and `brew uninstall` a package you don’t need.

/usr/local/Cellar.note: Don’t delete folders in the Cellar by hand: Homebrew links each installed version into its `bin` and other folders. `brew cleanup` removes old versions, and `brew uninstall` a package you don’t need.

~/Library/Safari.note: Don’t delete `~/Library/Safari` to save space: it holds your bookmarks and history along with site data. Clear the cache from Safari’s own settings.

~/Library/Containers/com.apple.Safari.note: Apple doesn’t document which file is which in Safari’s folders, so the safe route is Safari’s own settings, not the folders.

~/Library/Application Support/Spotify.note: Don’t delete this folder to clear the cache: it’s Spotify’s data folder, so downloads and settings saved on this Mac would go with it. Use Clear cache in Spotify’s settings.

~/.vscode/extensions.note: Uninstall extensions you don’t use from VS Code. Only a folder for an older version of an extension, one VS Code no longer uses, can go by hand, with VS Code quit.

~/Movies/iMovie Library.imovielibrary.note: That’s the whole iMovie library, a package iMovie manages. Delete render files with iMovie’s own Delete button: removing files inside by hand can break your projects.

~/Movies/<library name>.fcpbundle.note: That’s the whole Final Cut Pro library. Delete render files from inside Final Cut Pro; don’t open the library and delete things inside by hand.

library-caches.note: Leave the `com.apple.…` folders to macOS: many are guarded, and they belong to system services rather than to apps you can quit.

final-cut-pro-render-files.note: That’s the whole Final Cut Pro library. Delete render files from inside Final Cut Pro; don’t open the library and delete things inside by hand.

imovie-render-files.note: That’s the whole iMovie library, a package iMovie manages. Delete render files with iMovie’s own Delete button: removing files inside by hand can break your projects.
